headline: Your bone age
body: is measured from the wrong bones

headline: Bone age
body: gets treated as one number describing your whole skeleton. | It is read from an X-ray of your **hand and wrist**. | One value, applied to your entire body.
punch: Skeletons do not run on one clock.

headline: Different bones
body: senesce at different times. | Growth plate senescence runs **earlier** in small bones. | Metacarpals and phalanges finish before femurs and tibias.
punch: The bones in your hand finish first.

headline: Which is backwards
body: from what you want. | The bones read for bone age are the ones furthest along. | The bones deciding your height are the ones with time left.
punch: You are measuring the finished work to estimate the unfinished.

headline: Human imaging
body: MRI of **958 people** aged 14 to 21. | Wrist, knee and ankle growth plates measured. | Fusion timing varied by site **within the same person**.
punch: One body. Several different closure dates.

headline: It also found
body: Pubertal stage predicted fusion far better than age did. | Correlation around **0.5 to 0.6** for stage. Weaker for chronological age. | Hormonal exposure drives it, not time elapsed.
punch: Your birthday is not the variable.

headline: And a two year gap
body: between the sexes. | Complete fusion happened about **two years earlier** in girls. | At every single site measured.

headline: So what is bone age
body: A useful clinical estimate. Not a physical fact. | It tells you roughly how much growth capacity is left. | It does not tell you what any individual bone is doing.
punch: Useful estimate. Not a measurement of your legs.

headline: What actually sets it
body: *GH and IGF-1* drive proliferation. They move height fast and bone age slowly. | *Thyroid hormone* is required for chondrocyte maturation. It sets the tempo. | *Estrogen* is the dominant driver of maturation and fusion.
punch: Three axes so far. Two to go.

headline: Androgens
body: do both things at once. | They raise growth velocity **and** accelerate skeletal maturation simultaneously. | You get taller faster while having less time left to do it in.
punch: Two effects. Opposite directions. One hormone.

headline: Which is the tradeoff
body: Anything speeding growth velocity through the androgen axis also spends skeletal maturation. | Optimising one number while ignoring the other is how people end up shorter. | This is not a side effect. It is the same mechanism.
punch: Growing faster and growing longer compete.

headline: So the question
body: is never how tall you are now. | It is how much proliferative capacity remains. | And a hand X-ray only estimates that.

headline: It's never over
body: Real mechanisms. Real citations. No protocols.
